allowlist.source_of_truth: named files resolve from disk; allowlisted trees resolve from `git ls-files` only, so an unnamed working-tree file can never be exported

named_exclusions.why: rejected hero drafts; provenance for the operator, not tool surface

named_exclusions.what: templates/ inside the installed WHEEL (the directory itself DOES export, see TREES)
named_exclusions.why: the wheel carries the TOOL; the repository carries the CONTENT. Shipping `templates/` inside the wheel would need it to be an importable package — an `__init__.py` in a directory whose only admitted suffixes are .json and .md — or a second copy of all 12 files under `grok_bot_ops/`, which is two sources of truth for the same bytes. Neither is worth it, because `git clone && bash install.sh` gives BOTH: `install.sh` run from a clone points the `gb-walk` launcher at the CLONE's producer, so the tour reads the clone's templates. A `curl | bash` install gets the CLI and a `gb-walk bots` that names the clone as its remediation rather than rendering an empty tour

THE PUBLIC TREE SHIPS THE TOOLING, NOT THE CORPUS — Joshua, 2026-09-12. These three are DATA: the 645-Bot scrape, the teaching-form measurement over 3,026 X posts, and our own claim set. They were briefly exported earlier the same day on the argument that a stranger's clone needs the corpus for `gb corpus`, `gb demand` and gb mirror's percentile baseline to answer at all, which is TRUE and is not the deciding question. The corpus is the asset; the tool is the thing being published. A clone therefore carries every verb and refuses the corpus-dependent ones by naming the command that produces the input — `gb-usecases.py` fetches the scrape from its public upstream without auth, so a stranger can build their own rather than be handed ours. personas/, templates/, fixtures/, library/ and plugin/ DO ship: those are inputs the verbs operate ON, not measurements of anything

named_exclusions.what: usecases/ — the 645-Bot population corpus. NOT an account measurement, and it SHOULD travel: what holds it back is a scanner hit, not a policy judgement
named_exclusions.why: it is a scrape of `elie222/botdirectory.ai` — 645 Bots built by other people, each already published by its own author with an `x.com` permalink. Nothing in it resolves to this deployment: no Bot id, no account number, no client. Its absence is the largest measured value gap in the split: a clone gets `gb corpus` and `gb mirror`'s percentile baseline as verbs with no data, so the 90-second wedge — rank YOUR fleet against 645 real Bots — cannot run for the only audience it was built for. (`gb demand` has a SECOND, independent blocker and this corpus alone would not revive it: `build()` in `bin/gb-demand.py:423` returns None without `market/` too, and `market/` carries `installed` and `my_templates` — this account's state — so it stays in the exclusion line above on merit.) MEASURED 2026-09-11: admitting it as a `.json` Tree (0.91 MB over two snapshots, +6.7% on a 13.68 MB export) makes this exporter REFUSE with 2 `home_path` hits — `usecases/2026-09-11T0504.json:13632` and `usecases/2026-09-11T0620.json:13722`, both the same scraped Cursor-forum blurb that quotes a Grok Bot sandbox path under a /home/ user. Neither hit is in `rows[]`; both sit in the curated `links[]` array the three corpus verbs never read, and the other four scan classes are clean across all 28 664 lines. THE FIX IS UPSTREAM IN THE DATA: the blurb enters at `surface/2026-09-11/extras/practitioner-index:809` and is copied into `links[]` by `bin/gb-usecases.py`. Narrowing `home_path` to let it past would also exempt every real sandbox path this account's own Bots could leak — a weaker scanner bought for 0.91 MB, which is never the trade. Re-add the Tree the day the corpus scans clean; `python3 bin/gb-export-public.py --out /tmp/x --no-git --json` is the whole check
